items.claim: Hettinger talks, Beazley concurrency talk, PEP 8, PEP 20, PEP index
GIL precisely: one lock, released around IO and by C extensions; threads help IO not CPU in default build; free-threaded builds (3.14+)
items.status: verified (k1_gil on 3.14 and 3.14t); corrected: free-threaded experimental from 3.13, supported from 3.14

items.claim: Three concurrency models and when each applies; costs (thread stacks, pickling, event-loop starvation)
asyncio in depth: coroutines are objects, event loop, await yields, TaskGroup and asyncio.timeout, cancellation, never block the loop (run_in_executor), async for/async with
C boundary: NumPy avoids the interpreter; NumPy on 10 elements slower than a loop, faster on 10 million
PEP 659 specialising adaptive interpreter, quickening, inline caches
Write a C or Rust extension: nanobind or PyO3, buffer protocol, GIL rules under free-threading
items.status: moved to the Rust page Part 2 (PyO3) and its alternatives table

items.claim: Trap: threads for CPU work in default build; blocking calls inside an event loop
